source.title: A predicted distribution for Galois groups of maximal unramified extensions
source.authors: Yuan Liu, Melanie Matchett Wood and David Zureick-Brown
readSections: arXiv v2 (21 July 2022, 58 pages; e-print SHA-256 4772603bc93a83b2cb6241a7d2896ef044ab7dae9fe333f384fee08a067f79d4, PDF SHA-256 7f1e85da49b23f80fc7abe9a68dbc5384ab216dfa5d55cd5e3223ba3268abed9), read in full from its TeX source on 2026-09-22: Part I §§2–7 and Part II §§8–12. Locators are v2 statement numbers and pages.

The published article is paywalled and was not read; its Publisher Correction (SHA-256 553910550d1a9ae992e4842af9c694735e42fe64190cca755eb95f62b5eddd43) only restyles references. Any change between v2 and the published text is therefore unchecked.

Checked in detail: Proposition 2.2, the embedding argument of Lemma 2.7, Lemmas 3.4–3.6 and Corollaries 3.8–3.10, Proposition 3.13, Lemma 3.17 and Proposition 3.22, the probability formula of Proposition 4.3 and Theorem 4.12, Lemma 5.10 and Theorem 5.12, the moment computation of Theorem 6.2, §7.1, Lemma 9.3, the trace-formula assembly of Theorem 1.4, Proposition 12.7, Lemma 12.10 and the comparison b(G,c,q,n) = b(Γ,Γ∖1,q,n). Liu–Wood 2020, Wood 2021 and Wewers were used as quoted.

summary: Liu, Wood and Zureick-Brown build a random-group model for Gal(K^#/K), the Galois group of the maximal unramified, split-at-∞, prime-to-(roots of unity·|Γ|) extension of a totally real Γ-extension K of Q or F_q(t). They prove two structural facts: Gal(K^#/K) is an admissible Γ-group (Proposition 2.2) and has Property E, lifting along non-split central Z/p extensions (Theorem 2.5, via embedding problems). They define the free admissible Γ-group 𝓕_n and random quotients 𝓕_n/[Y(S)] by n+1 Haar-random relations, which is exactly the class of Property-E quotients (Proposition 3.13). As n → ∞ these converge to a probability measure μ_Γ with explicit values on basic opens (Theorem 1.2, via Theorem 4.12, chief factor pairs and Theorem 5.12). Its moments are E|Sur_Γ(X, H)| = [H : H^Γ]^{−1} (Theorem 6.2), and it abelianizes to Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet and pro-p-completes to Boston–Bush–Hajir (§7). They conjecture that Gal(K^#/K) is μ_Γ-distributed (Conjecture 1.3) and prove every moment in the q → ∞ function-field limit (Theorem 1.4; Corollary 1.5 for class groups). The proof counts Frobenius-fixed components of Hurwitz schemes with the Ellenberg–Venkatesh–Westerland/Wood lifting invariant (Theorem 10.4, §§10–12). The atlas has free profinite groups (ProfiniteProPGroups), the point-count trace formula and weight bounds (SF.2, EDC.2, DWP.7), Hurwitz schemes and embedding problems (IG.4–IG.5), function-field statistics (ST.5) and, via PAPER-WOOD-19, a proposed reduced-Schur Part II. It has nothing on random Γ-groups. The random-group theory (§§1–7) becomes a new Part II of Arithmetic statistics. The Galois facts go to IG.4, the Hurwitz and component machinery to IG.5 (stable braid orbits to IG.3), the reduced-multiplier group theory to the WOOD-19 candidate, the function-field moment theorem to ST.5, and a lattice-point lemma to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.4. The extraction recorded four source issues, all in arXiv v2 (the published text could not be read): a wrong equation reference in the proof of Theorem 4.12, 'N(E, …)' for N(H, …) in the proof of Theorem 1.4, (Z_p[Γ])^n for the augmentation-ideal lattice in §7.1, and Theorem 5.12 stated only for u ≥ 0 while later results use every integer u. The independent review confirmed them and added twenty-five. The main ones: the explicit limit formula (4.14), (5.13) and Theorem 5.15 is false for H without Property E, whose measure is 0 (E5). The inner limit in q of Theorem 1.4 is not shown to exist, so it is read as lim sup and lim inf (E6). Lemma 9.3 is off by [Γ : Z(Γ)] when E_Γ counts isomorphism classes (E7), and Lemma 12.8 needs positive weights (E8). The rest are proof gaps and misprints. None changes the moments or the main theorems' values.

items.name: Admissible Γ-groups, level-𝒞 completions and the space 𝒫
items.statement: Γ is a finite group; a Γ-group is a profinite group with a continuous Γ-action; Sur_Γ, Hom_Γ, Aut_Γ are Γ-equivariant maps; for a generating set γ_1, …, γ_d of Γ, Y : G → G^d, g ↦ (g^{−1}γ_1(g), …, g^{−1}γ_d(g)). G is admissible if it is topologically generated by {g^{−1}γ(g) : g ∈ G, γ ∈ Γ} and has order (supernatural) prime to |Γ|. For a set 𝒞 of finite Γ-groups, 𝒞̄ is its closure under finite products, Γ-subgroups and Γ-quotients, and G^𝒞 = lim G/M over closed normal Γ-subgroups with G/M ∈ 𝒞̄ (a functor to level-𝒞 groups preserving surjections). 𝒫 is the set of isomorphism classes of admissible |Γ|′-Γ-groups with all G^𝒞 finite, topologized by the basic opens U_{𝒞,H} = {X : X^𝒞 ≅ H}. A finite abelian |Γ|′-Γ-group is admissible iff H^Γ = 1 (§7.1).
items.locator: §1.2, p. 2; §1.7, p. 9; the pro-𝒞 completion (3.11), p. 15; 𝒫 and U_{𝒞,H} before Definition 3.15, p. 16; §7.1, p. 34
items.note: The basic notions of the random-group theory. The introduction defines U_{𝒞,H} = {G : G^𝒞 ≅ H^𝒞} for any finite Γ-group H; §3.2 uses {X : X^𝒞 ≅ H} with H of level 𝒞. The two agree for H of level 𝒞.

items.name: Theorem 1.2: the limiting distribution μ_Γ
items.statement: For every finite group Γ there is a probability measure μ_Γ on the set of isomorphism classes of admissible Γ-groups (on 𝒫) such that, as n → ∞, the distributions of X_{Γ,n} = 𝓕_n/[Y(S)] (S = n+1 Haar-random elements of the free admissible Γ-group 𝓕_n) converge weakly to μ_Γ. Explicitly (5.13), for 𝒞 a finite set of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups and H a finite admissible Γ-group of level 𝒞 that has Property E in the category of level-𝒞 Γ-groups, μ_Γ(U_{𝒞,H}) = |Aut_Γ(H)|^{−1}[H : H^Γ]^{−1} ∏_{G∈𝒜_H} ∏_{i≥1}(1 − λ(𝒞,H,G) h_{H⋊Γ}(G)^{−i}/[G : G^Γ]) ∏_{G∈𝒩} e^{−λ(𝒞,H,G)/[G:G^Γ]}. Here λ(𝒞,H,G) = (h_{H⋊Γ}(G) − 1) Σ_{(E,π)∈𝓔_𝒞(G,H)} |Aut_{Γ,H}(E,π)|^{−1} for G ∈ 𝒜_H and Σ_{(E,π)∈𝓔_𝒞(G,H)} |Aut_{Γ,H}(E,π)|^{−1} for G ∈ 𝒩, with h_{H⋊Γ}(G) = |Hom_{H⋊Γ}(G,G)|. If H lacks Property E at level 𝒞, then μ_Γ(U_{𝒞,H}) = 0; the printed (5.13) omits this case and is wrong there (sourceIssues E5).
items.locator: Theorem 1.2, p. 2 (arXiv v2), proof in §5.3, p. 30
items.note: μ_Γ = μ_1. Weak convergence comes from the Carathéodory extension (Theorem 5.12) and Fatou on open sets: μ_Γ(U) ≤ liminf_n μ_{1,n}(U), which the text writes as lim (E14). This is the Portmanteau criterion. The value 0 for H without Property E holds because every (X_{u,n})^𝒞 has Property E (Proposition 3.13, item 14).

items.name: Conjecture 1.3: Gal(K^#/K) is distributed according to μ_Γ
items.statement: Q is Q or F_q(t); Δ = 2|Γ| for Q = Q and Δ = q(q−1)|Γ| for F_q(t); for a Γ-extension K/Q, K^# is the maximal extension of K unramified everywhere, split completely above ∞, with all finite subextensions of degree prime to Δ. Let q be prime to |Γ|, 𝒞 a finite set of finite Γ-groups of order prime to Δ and H a finite admissible such group. With E_Γ(D, Q) the totally real Γ-extensions with radical discriminant norm rD(K) = D: lim_B Σ_{D≤B} #{K ∈ E_Γ(D,Q) : Gal(K^#/K)^𝒞 ≅ H^𝒞} / Σ_{D≤B} |E_Γ(D,Q)| = μ_Γ(U_{𝒞,H}), and lim_B Σ_{D≤B} Σ_K |Sur_Γ(Gal(K^#/K), H)| / Σ_{D≤B} |E_Γ(D,Q)| = ∫ |Sur_Γ(X, H)| dμ_Γ = [H : H^Γ]^{−1}.
items.locator: Conjecture 1.3, p. 3 (arXiv v2)
items.note: A conjecture, recorded as a statement. It implies the Cohen–Martinet predictions (prime-to-|Γ| parts, fields ordered by radical discriminant) and the Boston–Bush–Hajir predictions for real quadratic fields.

items.name: Theorem 1.4: function-field moments as q → ∞
items.statement: Let Γ be finite and H a finite admissible Γ-group. For prime powers q with (q, |Γ||H|) = 1 and (q−1, |H|) = 1, let R_b(q) = Σ_{n≤b} Σ_{K∈E_Γ(q^n,F_q(t))} |Sur_Γ(Gal(K^#/K), H)| / Σ_{n≤b} |E_Γ(q^n,F_q(t))|. Then lim_{b→∞} lim sup_{q→∞} R_b(q) = lim_{b→∞} lim inf_{q→∞} R_b(q) = ∫ |Sur_Γ(X,H)| dμ_Γ(X) = [H : H^Γ]^{−1}. The paper writes lim_{b→∞} lim_{q→∞}, but the proof shows only that for each b every limit point in q lies within O_G(1/b) of [H : H^Γ]^{−1} (sourceIssues E6).
items.locator: Theorem 1.4, p. 3 (arXiv v2), proof in §10.2, pp. 40–41
items.note: Proof: Lemma 9.3 (count of surjections), Lemma 10.2 (F_q-points of Hurwitz schemes), Lemma 10.3 with Grothendieck–Lefschetz and Deligne's bound, Theorem 10.4 (Frobenius-fixed components), and Theorem 6.2 (u = 1). The hypotheses force |H| odd (q or q − 1 is even); the paper refers to Wood 2019 for even |H|. The last step of the proof replaces Gal(K^{un,∞}/K) (Lemma 9.3) by Gal(K^#/K). This is valid because |H| is prime to q(q−1)|Γ|, so every Γ-surjection onto H factors through Gal(K^#/K).

items.name: Corollary 1.5: Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet moments over F_q(t)
items.statement: Let H be a finite abelian Γ-group with (|H|, |Γ|) = 1 and H^Γ = 1. Then, with q running over prime powers with (q,|Γ||H|) = 1 and (q−1,|H|) = 1, lim_{b} lim sup_{q→∞} and lim_{b} lim inf_{q→∞} of Σ_{n≤b} Σ_{K∈E_Γ(q^n,F_q(t))} |Sur_Γ(Cl(O_K), H)| / Σ_{n≤b} |E_Γ(q^n,F_q(t))| both equal |H|^{−1} (the paper writes lim_b lim_q; see sourceIssues E6).
items.locator: Corollary 1.5, p. 4 (arXiv v2)
items.note: Gal(K^#/K)^ab is the prime-to-q(q−1)|Γ| part of Cl(O_K) by class field theory. These are the Cohen–Lenstra/Cohen–Martinet averages, with fields ordered by radical discriminant; by Wang–Wood the moments determine the distribution.

items.name: Definition 2.1: the Γ-action on Gal(K^#/K)
items.statement: Q is Q or F_q(t); Δ = 2|Γ| for Q = Q and Δ = q(q−1)|Γ| for F_q(t); for a Γ-extension K/Q, K^# is the maximal extension of K unramified everywhere, split completely above ∞, with all finite subextensions of degree prime to Δ. For a pro-|Γ|′ extension L/K Galois over Q, a section s : Γ → Gal(L/Q) (Schur–Zassenhaus) gives Gal(L/Q) ≅ Gal(L/K) ⋊ Γ and a Γ-action on Gal(L/K), well defined up to isomorphism because all sections are conjugate. Definition 2.1 fixes such a section for K^#.
items.locator: Definition 2.1, p. 10 (arXiv v2), and the preceding paragraph, p. 10
items.note: Conjugacy of all complements in the coprime case is the Schur–Zassenhaus theorem; in general its proof uses Feit–Thompson (see the Schur–Zassenhaus item).

items.name: Proposition 2.2: unramified Galois groups are admissible
items.statement: Let K be a Γ-extension of Q and L an unramified pro-|Γ|′ extension of K, Galois over Q and split completely above ∞. Then Gal(L/K) is an admissible Γ-group.
items.locator: Proposition 2.2, p. 10 (arXiv v2)
items.note: The Γ-coinvariant quotient Ḡ gives an unramified Ḡ-extension of Q split at ∞, hence trivial (Minkowski for Q; for F_q(t), the absence of such extensions). PAPER-WOOD-19 routes the same 'no unramified split-infinity extension of the base' input to IG.4.

items.name: Definition 2.3: Property E
items.statement: For a full subcategory C of Γ-groups, H ∈ C has Property E if for every non-split central extension 1 → Z/pZ → G̃ → G → 1 in C (p prime, trivial Γ-action on Z/pZ), every Γ-surjection H → G lifts to a Γ-surjection H → G̃.
items.locator: Definition 2.3, p. 11 (arXiv v2)
items.note: Group-theoretic; the random-group Part II owns it.

items.name: Theorem 2.5 with Lemmas 2.6–2.7: Gal(K^#/K) has Property E
items.statement: Q is Q or F_q(t); Δ = 2|Γ| for Q = Q and Δ = q(q−1)|Γ| for F_q(t); for a Γ-extension K/Q, K^# is the maximal extension of K unramified everywhere, split completely above ∞, with all finite subextensions of degree prime to Δ. For every Γ-extension K/Q, Gal(K^#/K) has Property E in the category of Δ′-Γ-groups. Lemma 2.6: for p prime to the order of the roots of unity in Q, local characters φ_v : Gal_{Q_v} → Z/p (almost all unramified) come from a global φ agreeing with φ_v on inertia at finite v and on Gal_{Q_∞}. Lemma 2.7: for G a |Γ|′-Γ-group, L/Q a (G⋊Γ)-extension with L/L^G unramified and split at ∞, p ∤ Δ, and a non-split central Γ-extension 1 → Z/p → G̃ → G → 1, there is L̃ ⊃ L with Gal(L̃/Q) ≅ G̃ ⋊ Γ compatibly, L̃/L^G unramified and split at ∞.
items.locator: Theorem 2.5, p. 11 (arXiv v2), Lemmas 2.6–2.7, pp. 11–13
items.note: An embedding-problem argument: local solutions with trivial inertia on N, the local–global principle for central embedding problems (Malle–Matzat Cor. 10.2), correction by a global character (Lemma 2.6; Serre, Topics, 2.1.6), and an inverse limit for profinite G. In the profinite step (p. 13), "for every open subgroup U" should read: every open normal Γ-stable U of G̃ with U ∩ N = 1 (E27).

items.name: Schur–Zassenhaus for profinite groups
items.statement: If K is a closed normal subgroup of a profinite group G with (#K, #G/K) = 1, then K has a complement, and all complements are conjugate (Ribes–Zalesskii, Theorem 2.3.15). Consequently, for H a finite |Γ|′-Γ-group, the sections of H⋊Γ → Γ form a single H-conjugacy orbit with stabilizer H^Γ, so there are [H : H^Γ] of them (used in Lemmas 3.4 and 9.3).
items.locator: §2, p. 10; proofs of Lemmas 3.4, 3.6, 5.2, 9.3 and Theorem 10.4 (Ribes–Zalesskii 2.3.15)
items.note: Mathlib proves existence for finite groups (Subgroup.exists_right_complement'_of_coprime), and conjugacy only in the abelian case (Subgroup.exists_smul_eq). The general conjugacy statement uses the Feit–Thompson theorem (one of the two coprime orders is odd) or a solvability hypothesis. Conjugacy is used from the start: surjectivity of the map Φ in §3.1 gives Lemma 3.4, hence Lemma 3.1 (admissibility of 𝓕_n and the retraction π) and Lemma 3.6(1). All of Part I, Definition 2.1 and Lemma 9.3 therefore depend on it. When Γ is solvable, or 𝓕_n is pro-odd, no Feit–Thompson is needed. Owned by the random-group Part II.

items.name: The free admissible Γ-group 𝓕_n and Lemma 3.1
items.statement: Γ is a finite group; a Γ-group is a profinite group with a continuous Γ-action; Sur_Γ, Hom_Γ, Aut_Γ are Γ-equivariant maps; for a generating set γ_1, …, γ_d of Γ, Y : G → G^d, g ↦ (g^{−1}γ_1(g), …, g^{−1}γ_d(g)). F_n(Γ) is the free pro-|Γ|′ group on {x_{i,γ} : 1 ≤ i ≤ n, γ ∈ Γ} with σ(x_{i,γ}) = x_{i,σγ}; 𝓕_n(Γ) is the closed Γ-subgroup generated by x_i^{−1}γ_j(x_i), x_i = x_{i,1}. Lemma 3.1: 𝓕_n is admissible, and there is a Γ-quotient map π : F_n → 𝓕_n with π ∘ (inclusion) = id. Remark 3.2: as a pro-|Γ|′ group 𝓕_n is free on {x_i^{−1}σ(x_i) : σ ≠ 1}; it is Γ-generated by n elements; and any pro-|Γ|′ Γ-group H that is generated by elements h_i^{−1}γ(h_i) (1 ≤ i ≤ n, γ ∈ Γ) is a quotient of 𝓕_n. The text omits "pro-|Γ|′" (sourceIssues E12).
items.locator: Lemma 3.1, p. 13 (arXiv v2), §3.1 and Remark 3.2, p. 13
items.note: Free pro-|Γ|′ groups on finite sets come from ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 4 (the planned item below).

items.name: Lemmas 3.4–3.6: the map Y and sections
items.statement: Γ is a finite group; a Γ-group is a profinite group with a continuous Γ-action; Sur_Γ, Hom_Γ, Aut_Γ are Γ-equivariant maps; for a generating set γ_1, …, γ_d of Γ, Y : G → G^d, g ↦ (g^{−1}γ_1(g), …, g^{−1}γ_d(g)). For a |Γ|′-Γ-group G, Y(G) is in bijection with the sections of G⋊Γ → Γ (the text says "for any Γ-group G", sourceIssues E12). Lemma 3.4: for a |Γ|′-Γ-group G and a closed Γ-subgroup E, Y(E) = Y(G) ∩ E^d. Lemma 3.5: for finite G, Y^{−1}(Y(g)) = G^Γ g, so |G| = |G^Γ||Y(G)|. Lemma 3.6: for 1 → N → G → H → 1 of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups, 1 → N^Γ → G^Γ → H^Γ → 1 is exact, |Y(N)| = |Y(G)|/|Y(H)|, and |Y(G) ∩ π^{−1}(x)| = |Y(G)|/|Y(H)| for x ∈ Y(H).
items.locator: Lemma 3.4, p. 14 (arXiv v2), Lemmas 3.5–3.6, p. 14
items.note: H¹(Γ, N) = 0 by Schur–Zassenhaus.

items.name: Corollary 3.8, Lemma 3.9 and Corollary 3.10: homomorphisms from 𝓕_n
items.statement: For any pro-|Γ|′ Γ-group G, Y(G)^n → Hom_Γ(𝓕_n, G), (Y(g_i)) ↦ (x_i ↦ g_i)|_{𝓕_n}, is a bijection (Corollary 3.8; the text says "for any Γ-group G", which fails for Γ = Z/2 acting on Z/4 by inversion, sourceIssues E12). An admissible G is Γ-generated by the coordinates of Y(G), so 𝓕_n is independent of the generating set of Γ (Lemma 3.9). 𝓕_n^{ab} ≅ (Z[Γ]/(Σ_g g))^n with Z = ∏_{p∤|Γ|} Z_p, and (𝓕_n^{ab})^Γ = 1 (Corollary 3.10).
items.locator: Corollary 3.8, p. 14 (arXiv v2), Lemma 3.9 and Corollary 3.10, pp. 14–15

items.name: Proposition 3.13 (with Lemma 3.12): Property E ⟺ relations of the form Y(r)
items.statement: Lemma 3.12: if G̃ is admissible and N a normal Γ-subgroup with trivial Γ-action, then G̃ acts trivially on N. Proposition 3.13: for a set 𝒞 of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups and a Γ-surjection φ : (𝓕_n)^𝒞 → H, ker φ = [Y(ker φ)] iff H has Property E in the category of level-𝒞 Γ-groups. In particular, every random group (X_{u,n})^𝒞 = (𝓕_n)^𝒞/[Y(S)] has Property E in the category of level-𝒞 Γ-groups.
items.locator: Proposition 3.13, p. 16 (arXiv v2), with Lemma 3.12, pp. 15–16
items.note: The motivation for taking relations Y(r). The "⟹" proof applies Lemma 3.6(2), a statement about finite groups, to ker ϖ, which is infinite when 𝒞 is. The direct argument works: Y(ker ϖ) ⊂ (ker ρ)^d, then Lemma 3.4 (E13).

items.name: Definition 3.15: the random groups X_{Γ,n,u} and the measures μ_{u,n}, μ_u
items.statement: For n ≥ 1 and u > −n, X_{Γ,n,u} = 𝓕_n/[Y(S)] with S a multiset of n+u independent Haar-random elements of 𝓕_n (u = 1 by default); μ_{n,u}(A) = Prob(X_{u,n} ∈ A) on Borel subsets of 𝒫, and μ_u(A) = lim_n μ_{n,u}(A) on the algebra generated by the basic opens (3.16). For finite 𝒞, (𝓕_n)^𝒞 is finite.
items.locator: Definition 3.15, p. 17 (arXiv v2), and (3.16), p. 17
items.note: The Haar probability measure on the compact group 𝓕_n is Mathlib's haarMeasure ⊤ (MeasureTheory.Measure.haarMeasure with haarMeasure_self). Measure.haar has an arbitrary normalization. The pro-𝒞 finiteness argument is the paper's.

items.name: Proposition 3.22 (with Lemma 3.17): p-class tower groups occur in the model
items.statement: Q is Q or F_q(t); Δ = 2|Γ| for Q = Q and Δ = q(q−1)|Γ| for F_q(t); for a Γ-extension K/Q, K^# is the maximal extension of K unramified everywhere, split completely above ∞, with all finite subextensions of degree prime to Δ. Let p ∤ Δ with μ_p ⊄ K, and let G_{K,p} be the maximal pro-p quotient of Gal(K^#/K). Lemma 3.17: in the notation of §3.3 there is an F_p[Γ]-surjection F_p[Γ]^{n+1} → N/N* (via Hochschild–Serre, Koch Theorem 11.3 and O_K^×/p ↪ F_p[Γ]/(Σ g)). Proposition 3.22: if G_{K,p} = [Y({h_1,…,h_n})], then G_{K,p} ≅ (𝓕_n)_p/[Y(S)] for some S ⊂ (𝓕_n)_p with |S| = n+1.
items.locator: Proposition 3.22, pp. 19–20 (arXiv v2), with Lemma 3.17, pp. 18–19
items.note: Uses the finite presentation of G_{K,p} (Koch, Chapter 11) and pro-p generation theory (NSW Corollary 3.9.3). The function-field case of the proof of Lemma 3.17 uses O_K^× = F_{q^r}^×. That is false when several places lie over ∞, as they do for every totally real K with Γ ≠ 1. The proof goes through with the complete curve, using constant units and Pic⁰(C_K)[p] (E11). The notation of §3.3 also has two slips (E21).

items.name: The fundamental short exact sequence and the multiplicities m(𝒞, n, H, G)
items.statement: For finite 𝒞, a Γ-surjection ϖ : (𝓕_n)^𝒞 → H with kernel N, and M the intersection of the maximal proper (𝓕_n)^𝒞-normal Γ-subgroups of N: 1 → R → F → H → 1 with F = (𝓕_n)^𝒞/M, R = N/M (4.1), induced by 1 → R → F⋊Γ → H⋊Γ → 1 (4.2); R is a product of irreducible F⋊Γ-groups. 𝒜_H is the set of non-trivial finite abelian irreducible |Γ|′-(H⋊Γ)-groups. "Non-trivial" refers to the group, so 𝒜_H contains Z/p with trivial H⋊Γ-action, for which |Y(G)| = 1 and 𝒩 the set of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups isomorphic to T^j (T non-abelian simple); m(𝒞, n, H, G) is the multiplicity of G in R (summed over the compatible F⋊Γ-structures for G ∈ 𝒩), independent of ϖ (Remark 4.9).

items.name: Proposition 4.3 and Remark 4.4: probability that Y-relations generate R
items.statement: For a Γ-group F and R = ∏ G_i^{m_i} with pairwise non-isomorphic finite irreducible F⋊Γ-groups G_i, and n+u ≥ 1 uniform random r_1, …, r_{n+u} ∈ R: Prob([Y({r_j})]_{F⋊Γ} = R) = ∏_{G_i abelian} ∏_{j=0}^{m_i−1}(1 − h_{F⋊Γ}(G_i)^j |Y(G_i)|^{−n−u}) ∏_{G_i non-abelian}(1 − |Y(G_i)|^{−n−u})^{m_i}, where h_G(H) = |Hom_G(H, H)|. Remark 4.4: for G abelian irreducible, h_{F⋊Γ}(G)^𝔪 = |Y(G)| with 𝔪 maximal such that G^𝔪 is generated by the coordinates of one Y(g).
items.locator: Proposition 4.3, p. 21 (arXiv v2), and Remark 4.4, p. 21
items.note: Uses Liu–Wood's Lemmas 5.5 and 5.8. The proof (p. 21) writes 𝓕_n for 𝓕_{n+u}, Y[(…)] for [Y(…)], and "γ ∈ F⋊Γ" for the F⋊Γ-subgroup generated by the y_i^{−1}γ(y_i), γ ∈ Γ (E22).

items.name: Lemma 4.6, Proposition 4.7 and Corollary 4.8: counting H-extensions
items.statement: An H-extension is a Γ-group E with a Γ-surjection π : E → H. It is admissible if E is, and a sub-H-extension is a Γ-subgroup E′ with π|_{E′} surjective. For G abelian irreducible, 𝓔(G, H) is the set of isomorphism classes of admissible H-extensions with ker π ≅ G as H⋊Γ-groups. For G non-abelian, it is the set with ker π ≅ G as Γ-groups and irreducible as an E⋊Γ-group. 𝓔_𝒞(G, H) is the subset with E of level 𝒞. Lemma 4.6: for ρ : (𝓕_n)^𝒞 → H and a finite H-extension (E, π), |Sur_{Γ,H}(ρ, π)| = Σ_{D∈𝓔^E_H} ν(D, E)(|Y(D)|/|Y(H)|)^n if E is admissible of level 𝒞, and 0 otherwise. Here ν is the Möbius function of the poset 𝓔^E_H of sub-H-extensions: ν(E, E) = 1 and ν(D, E) = −Σ_{D ⊊ D′ ⊆ E} ν(D′, E). The printed recursion omits D ⊊ D′ (sourceIssues E9). Proposition 4.7 counts |Sur_{F⋊Γ}(R, G)| over 𝓔_𝒞(G, H). Corollary 4.8: for G ∈ 𝒜_H, (h_{H⋊Γ}(G)^m − 1)/(h_{H⋊Γ}(G) − 1) = Σ_{(E,π)∈𝓔_𝒞(G,H)} Σ_D ν(D,E)(|Y(D)|/|Y(H)|)^n / |Aut_{Γ,H}(E,π)|, and for G ∈ 𝒩, m equals the same sum.
items.locator: Lemma 4.6, p. 22 (arXiv v2), Proposition 4.7 and Corollary 4.8, pp. 22–23
items.note: Uses Liu–Wood's Theorem 7.1 and Proposition 8.7.

items.name: Theorem 4.12: the measures of basic opens and their limits
items.statement: Let 𝒞 be a finite set of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups and H a finite admissible level-𝒞 Γ-group; n ≥ 1, u > −n. Then Prob((X_{u,n})^𝒞 ≅ H) = |Sur_Γ(𝓕_n, H)| / (|Aut_Γ(H)||Y(H)|^{n+u}) · ∏_{G∈𝒜_H} ∏_{k=0}^{m−1}(1 − h_{H⋊Γ}(G)^k/|Y(G)|^{n+u}) ∏_{G∈𝒩}(1 − |Y(G)|^{−n−u})^m (m = m(𝒞,n,H,G)) (4.13). If H has Property E in the category of level-𝒞 Γ-groups, the limit as n → ∞ is |Aut_Γ(H)|^{−1}|Y(H)|^{−u} ∏_{G∈𝒜_H} ∏_{i≥1}(1 − λ(𝒞,H,G) h_{H⋊Γ}(G)^{−i}/|Y(G)|^u) ∏_{G∈𝒩} e^{−|Y(G)|^{−u}λ(𝒞,H,G)} (4.14). Otherwise the probability is 0 for every n. Here λ(𝒞,H,G) = (h_{H⋊Γ}(G) − 1) Σ_{(E,π)∈𝓔_𝒞(G,H)} |Aut_{Γ,H}(E,π)|^{−1} for G ∈ 𝒜_H (4.10) and Σ_{(E,π)∈𝓔_𝒞(G,H)} |Aut_{Γ,H}(E,π)|^{−1} for G ∈ 𝒩 (4.11), with h_{H⋊Γ}(G) = |Hom_{H⋊Γ}(G,G)|. Only finitely many factors are non-trivial.
items.locator: Theorem 4.12, p. 24 (arXiv v2), with (4.10)–(4.11); proof as corrected by E1
items.note: Uses Liu–Wood's Corollary 6.12, Lemma 6.1 and Lemma 8.11. The proof cites the fundamental sequence as (7.1); it is (4.1) (E1). The printed (4.14) has no Property E hypothesis. It is false when H lacks Property E: then some G ∈ 𝒜_H with trivial Γ-action has λ ≠ 0, the step (4.17) fails for it (h^m = 1 + λ with m constant in n), and the limit formula is non-zero, sometimes negative, while (4.13) gives 0 (E5). Under Property E every G with λ ≠ 0 has |Y(G)| ≥ 2, and the proof is right.

items.name: Definition 5.1, Lemma 5.2 and Corollary 5.3: Γ-chief factor pairs
items.statement: For a finite |Γ|′-Γ-group G, CF_Γ(G) is the set of isomorphism classes of chief factor pairs (M, A) ∈ CF(G⋊Γ) with gcd(|M|, |Γ|) = 1, and CF_Γ(𝒞) = ∪_{G∈𝒞} CF_Γ(G). Lemma 5.2: if 𝒞 is closed under Γ-subgroups and Γ-quotients then CF_Γ(𝒞̄) = CF_Γ(𝒞). Corollary 5.3: if all groups in 𝒞 have order ≤ ℓ, then for (M, A) ∈ CF_Γ(𝒞̄) the prime-to-|Γ| part of |A/Inn(M)| is < ℓ, and CF_Γ(𝒞̄) is finite.
items.locator: Definition 5.1, p. 26 (arXiv v2), Lemma 5.2 and Corollary 5.3, pp. 26–27
items.note: Extends Liu–Wood's chief factor pairs (Lemmas 6.3, 6.11 and 6.13) to Γ-groups.

items.name: Lemma 5.4 and Corollary 5.9: multiplicity bounds at level ℓ
items.statement: Let 𝒞_ℓ be the set of |Γ|′-Γ-groups of order ≤ ℓ (the text omits |Γ|′, sourceIssues E18). Let H be of level 𝒞_ℓ and H̃ = H^{𝒞_{ℓ−1}}. The number of G ∈ 𝒜_H isomorphic to a given abelian M with some m(𝒞_ℓ, n, H, G) ≠ 0 is at most Σ_{(M,A)∈CF_Γ(𝒞̄_ℓ)} |Sur(H̃⋊Γ, A)|. The number of level-𝒞_ℓ H-extensions whose kernel M, a power of a non-abelian simple group, is an irreducible E⋊Γ-group is at most Σ |Sur(H̃⋊Γ, A/Inn(M))|. The text says "irred. E-group" (E19) (Lemma 5.4). Let P_{u,n}(U_{𝒞_ℓ,H}) be the product ∏_{G∈𝒜_H} ∏_{k<m}(1 − h_{H⋊Γ}(G)^k/|Y(G)|^{n+u}) ∏_{G∈𝒩}(1 − |Y(G)|^{−n−u})^m of (4.13), without its prefactor (p. 28). For ℓ > 1 there is c(u, ℓ, H̃) > 0, independent of n and of H over H̃, such that for all n ≥ 1 with u > −n, P_{u,n}(U_{𝒞_ℓ,H}) = 0 or P_{u,n}(U_{𝒞_ℓ,H}) ≥ c(u, ℓ, H̃) (Corollary 5.9).
items.locator: Lemma 5.4, p. 27 (arXiv v2), proof p. 28, and Corollary 5.9, pp. 28–29
items.note: Corollary 5.9 follows Liu–Wood Lemma 9.5. Chief factor pairs (M, A) and CF(G) are Liu–Wood's (LW20 §6), recalled on pp. 25–26.

items.name: Lemma 5.10: interchanging limits and sums over the level tower
items.statement: Let f_n(H, ℓ) ≥ 0 be defined for finite Γ-groups H of level 𝒞_ℓ. Assume: (1) f_n = g_n · P_{u,n}(U_{𝒞_ℓ,H}); (2) g_n(H, ℓ) → g(H, ℓ) and g_n ≤ g for every n; (3) Σ_{H over H̃} f_n(H, ℓ) = f_n(H̃, ℓ−1). Assume also that f_n(H, ℓ) > 0 implies f_{n′}(H, ℓ) > 0 for all n′ ≥ n. This hypothesis is not in the text; its proof needs it, and it holds in both applications (sourceIssues E10). Then lim_n f_n(H, ℓ) exists and Σ_H lim_n f_n(H, ℓ) = lim_n f_n(1, 1). For u < 0, everything is read for n > −u.
items.locator: Lemma 5.10, p. 29 (arXiv v2)
items.note: By induction on ℓ and dominated convergence (Tannery's theorem), using Corollary 5.9. In the applications, positivity is monotone because killing x_{n+1} gives 𝓕_{n+1}/[Y(S̃ ∪ {y})] ≅ 𝓕_n/[Y(S)] with Y(y) = Y(x_{n+1}), and the event is open.

items.name: Theorem 5.12: countable additivity of μ_u
items.statement: For every integer u, μ_u is countably additive on the algebra generated by the basic opens U_{𝒞,H}, hence extends uniquely to a Borel probability measure on 𝒫.
items.locator: Theorem 5.12, p. 30 (arXiv v2), statement as corrected by E4
items.note: Printed for u ≥ 0 only, although Theorems 5.15, 6.2 and 7.4 use μ_u for all u. The proof (Lemma 5.10 with f_n = μ_{u,n}(U_{𝒞_ℓ,H})) never uses u ≥ 0 (E4). For u < 0, X_{u,n} is defined only for n > −u, and Lemma 5.10 is applied to those n. The reduction to Σ_H μ_u(U_{𝒞_ℓ,H}) = 1 is Liu–Wood's Corollary 9.7 and Theorem 9.1. The proof's "g(H) = |Aut_Γ(H)|^{−1}|Y(H)|^{−u} by Corollary 3.8" is for admissible H and also uses (4.18); for other H, g = 0.

items.name: Definition 5.14 and Theorem 5.15: μ_u on V_{𝒞,H} for arbitrary 𝒞
items.statement: For any set 𝒞 of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups, finite admissible H of level 𝒞 with Property E in the category of level-𝒞 Γ-groups, and integer u, with m and λ extended to infinite 𝒞 as limits over an exhausting chain 𝒟_1 ⊂ 𝒟_2 ⊂ ⋯ (Definition 5.14): μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) = μ_u({X : X^𝒞 ≅ H}) = |Aut_Γ(H)|^{−1}|Y(H)|^{−u} ∏_{G∈𝒜_H} ∏_{i≥1}(1 − λ(𝒞,H,G) h_{H⋊Γ}(G)^{−i}/|Y(G)|^u) ∏_{G∈𝒩} e^{−|Y(G)|^{−u}λ(𝒞,H,G)}. If H lacks Property E at level 𝒞, then μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) = 0. The printed theorem has no Property E hypothesis and is false for such H (sourceIssues E5).
items.locator: Theorem 5.15, p. 31 (arXiv v2), with Definition 5.14, p. 31
items.note: As in Liu–Wood Lemma 11.3. m and λ are nondecreasing and bounded along 𝒟_i, and V_{𝒞,H} = ∩_i U_{𝒟_i,H} for large i. The proof uses continuity from above, which needs Theorem 5.12 for every u (E4). Example of the failure: Γ = Z/2, p = 3, 𝒞 all finite 3-Γ-groups, H = F_3² with σ = −1. The printed formula gives 2.70·10^{−3} at u = 0, while Theorem 7.4 gives 0.

items.name: Lemma 6.1 and Theorem 6.2: the moments of μ_u
items.statement: For a finite admissible |Γ|′-Γ-group A and any integer u: lim_n E|Sur_Γ(X_{u,n}, A)| = [A : A^Γ]^{−u} (Lemma 6.1), and if X_u has distribution μ_u then E|Sur_Γ(X_u, A)| = [A : A^Γ]^{−u} (Theorem 6.2). In particular the μ_Γ-moment is [A : A^Γ]^{−1}.
items.locator: Lemma 6.1, p. 31 (arXiv v2); Theorem 6.2, pp. 32–33
items.note: The interchange of limit and sum uses Lemma 5.10 with f_n(H, ℓ) = E(|Sur_Γ(X_{u,n}, A)| · 1_{X^{𝒞_ℓ} ≅ H}). For u = 0 these are Boston–Wood's imaginary-quadratic moments.

items.name: §7.1: abelianization gives the Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet distribution
items.statement: For 𝒞 the abelian |Γ|′-Γ-groups and finite abelian H with H^Γ = 1: m(𝒞, n, H, G) = n𝔪_G and λ(𝒞, H, G) = 1 for G with trivial H-action and G^Γ = 1 (for the trivial Γ-representation, m = 0 and λ = 0), and μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) = |Aut_Γ(H)|^{−1}|H|^{−u} ∏_{p∤|Γ|} ∏_{G nontrivial irreducible F_p[Γ]-rep} ∏_{i≥1}(1 − h_Γ(G)^{−i}/|G|^u). For u = 1 this is the Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet prediction for prime-to-|Γ| class groups of totally real Γ-fields (u = 0, 1 and Γ = Z/2: imaginary/real quadratic).
items.locator: §7.1, p. 34; as corrected by E3
items.note: Uses that finite-index Γ-submodules N_p of (𝓕_n)^𝒞_p ≅ (Z_p[Γ]/(Σ g))^n are isomorphic to it (Z_p[Γ] hereditary; Serre, Linear representations §16 Thm 34). The text writes (Z_p[Γ])^n (E3). Agreement with Cohen–Martinet in Wang–Wood's Proposition 6.5. The text's "h_Γ(G)^{𝔪_G} = |G| for each G ∈ 𝒜_H" needs G^Γ = 1 (Remark 4.4 gives |Y(G)|). That holds for every G occurring here, since F^Γ = 1.

items.name: Lemma 7.2 and Theorems 7.4–7.5: Boston–Bush–Hajir distributions
items.statement: Let Γ = Z/2, p odd, 𝒞 the finite p-Γ-groups (or those of p-class ≤ c). For H of the form 𝓕_n^𝒞/[Y(S)] with |S| = n+u: μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) = |Aut_Γ(H)|^{−1}|Y(H)|^{−u} ∏_{i≥1+u+d(H)−r(H)}(1 − p^{−i}) (Theorem 7.4; d, r the generator and relation ranks), and for p-class c the same with r(H) replaced by r(H) − ν(H) when cl_p(H) = c (ν the nuclear rank) (Theorem 7.5); otherwise μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) = 0. For u = 0, 1 these are the Boston–Bush–Hajir measures for imaginary and real quadratic fields. Lemma 7.2 identifies the fundamental sequence with the p-covering-group sequence (7.1).
items.locator: Theorem 7.4, p. 35 (arXiv v2), Lemma 7.2, Remark 7.3 and Theorem 7.5, pp. 34–37
items.note: Uses Liu–Wood Lemma 12.5. For n = d(H), (7.1) is the p-covering group sequence 1 → R′ → F′ → H → 1. R′ is the p-multiplicator, of dimension r(H); the text calls R′ the "p-multiplicator rank" (E24). The nucleus is P_c(F′), the last non-trivial term of the lower p-central series of F′ when cl_p(H) = c, and ν(H) = dim_{F_p} P_c(F′) is the nuclear rank (p. 36). The u = 0 comparison is Boston–Wood Lemma 4.8.

items.name: Lemmas 9.1 and 9.3: counting unramified H-extensions via H⋊Γ-extensions
items.statement: Lemma 9.1: for a Γ-group H and profinite G, Sur(G, H⋊Γ) is in bijection with tuples (ρ ∈ Sur(G, Γ), N closed normal ⊂ ker ρ, section s : Γ → G/N, φ ∈ Isom_Γ(ker ρ/N, H)). Lemma 9.3: let H be a finite |Γ|′-Γ-group and let K^{un,∞} be the maximal extension of K unramified everywhere and split completely above ∞. Let N(H, Γ, D, Q) count the surjections Gal(Q̄/Q) → H⋊Γ whose H-extension is unramified and split above ∞, whose Γ-extension is split at ∞, and with rD = D. Then Σ_K |Sur_Γ(Gal(K^{un,∞}/K)^{|Γ|′}, H)| = [H : H^Γ]^{−1} N(H, Γ, D, Q). Here K runs over the surjections Gal(Q̄/Q) → Γ with the conditions, i.e. over Γ-extensions K ⊂ Q̄ with their identification, not up to isomorphism. Read with E_Γ(D, Q) as isomorphism classes (p. 3), the right-hand side must be multiplied by |Z(Γ)|/|Γ| (sourceIssues E7). The Γ-action is defined on the maximal pro-|Γ|′ quotient (Definition 2.1; the text writes Gal(K^{un,∞}/K), E28).
items.locator: Lemma 9.1, pp. 37–38 (arXiv v2), and Lemma 9.3, p. 38 (proof pp. 38–39)
items.note: The factor [H : H^Γ] is the number of sections (Schur–Zassenhaus conjugacy). The normalization of E_Γ cancels in the moment ratios of Conjecture 1.3 and Theorem 1.4.

items.name: Hurwitz stacks and schemes: Hur^n_G, Hur^n_{G,1}, Hur^n_{G,*}, 𝓗ur^n_{G,c}
items.statement: Hur^n_G is the stack of tame Galois covers X → P^1_S with n branch points and G ≅ Aut; Theorem 11.1 (Wewers): it is a separated DM stack, smooth of finite type over Z with coarse scheme, and the branch-locus map to Conf^n(P^1) is étale, and proper over Z[1/|G|]. Hur^n_{G,1} adds a point over ∞ (algebraic, separated, with coarse scheme; Lemma 11.2); Hur^n_{G,*} requires that point unramified: it is a scheme, finite étale over Conf^n(A^1)_{Z[1/|G|]} (Proposition 11.4). For G, c as in Notation 10.1 (c a conjugation- and invertible-power-stable generating subset of G∖1), 𝓗ur^n_{G,c} is the union of components of (Hur^n_{G,*})_{Z[1/|G|]} whose inertia groups are generated by elements of c (component-constant by Wood's Theorem 3.1 and Remark 5.3).
items.locator: Theorem 11.1, p. 42 (arXiv v2), Lemma 11.2, Remark 11.3, Proposition 11.4 and §11.4, pp. 41–45
items.note: PAPER-WOOD-19 and PAPER-ELLENBERG-VENKATESH-WESTERLAND-16 route the marked Hurwitz scheme to IG.5.

items.name: Proposition 11.5, Remark 11.6 and Theorem 11.7: analytic and topological Hurwitz spaces
items.statement: Hall's relative GAGA (a morphism of analytic stacks inducing equivalences on local Artinian points is an equivalence) and stacky GAGA give equivalences (Hur^n_G)_an ≃ Hur^{n,an}_G and (Hur^n_{G,*})_an ≃ Hur^{n,an}_{G,*} (Theorem 11.7). Hur^{n,an}_{G,*} is isomorphic to the topological Hurwitz space Hur^{n,top}_{G,*}, a covering space of Conf^n(A^1)(C) (§11.3).
items.locator: Theorem 11.7, p. 44 (arXiv v2), Proposition 11.5, Remark 11.6 and §11.3, pp. 43–45
items.note: Uses Artin's algebraization of formal moduli II (Theorem 7.3) and Knutson.

items.name: Lemma 10.2: F_q-points of 𝓗ur^n_{G,c} count the extensions
items.statement: Let H be a finite |Γ|′-Γ-group, G = H⋊Γ and c the non-identity elements of G of the same order as their image in Γ. The text omits "non-identity" (sourceIssues E17), and Notation 10.1 needs c ⊂ G ∖ 1 to generate G, which holds when H is admissible, as in all uses. For q prime to |G| and n ≥ 0, |𝓗ur^n_{G,c}(F_q)| = N(H, Γ, q^n, F_q(t)).
items.locator: Lemma 10.2, p. 39 (arXiv v2), proof pp. 45–46
items.note: Split completely at ∞ forces constant field F_q, so the covers are geometrically connected; rD(K) = q^{deg branch divisor}. The last line of the proof writes N(H, Γ, n, F_q(t)) for N(H, Γ, q^n, F_q(t)) (E16).

items.name: Lemma 10.3: cohomology comparison for components
items.statement: For a connected component Y of 𝓗ur^n_{G,c}, i ≥ 0, q prime to |G| and primes ℓ ∤ q, ℓ > n: Y_{F̄_q} is smooth of dimension n and dim H^i_{c,ét}(Y_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ) = dim H^{2n−i}(Y_C, Q).
items.locator: Lemma 10.3, p. 39 (arXiv v2), proof p. 46
items.note: Poincaré duality, EVW Proposition 7.7 (upgraded from Z/ℓ to Q_ℓ coefficients) on the ordered-configuration cover, S_n-invariants, and the Artin comparison. The comparison is PAPER-ELLENBERG-VENKATESH-WESTERLAND-16/68 (Proposition 7.7) on the ordered-configuration compactification (/66). The hypothesis ℓ > n matters only for Z/ℓ coefficients.

items.name: Lemma 11.8: Frobenius on Hurwitz points
items.statement: For q prime to |G|, Frob of (𝓗ur^n_{G,c})_{F_q} sends the F̄_q-point (f, ι, P) to its base change (f^F, ι^F, P^F) along F : x ↦ x^q.
items.locator: Lemma 11.8, p. 46 (arXiv v2)
items.note: The proof's "Frob_Z ∘ s = s ∘ F" holds in Z(F̄_q) = Hom_{F_q}(Spec F̄_q, Z), i.e. after composing with Z_{F̄_q} → Z. As F̄_q-morphisms the two sides lie over different maps (E29).

items.name: Reduced multiplier H_2(G, c), the groups U(G, c), K(G, c) and the powering action
items.statement: For G, c as in Notation 10.1: Q_c ⊂ H_2(G, Z) is generated by ⟨x, y⟩ for x ∈ c, y commuting with x; H_2(G, c) = H_2(G, Z)/Q_c; S̄ = S/τ_S(Q_c) for a Schur cover S, with H_2(G, c) ≅ ker(S̄ → G); U(G, c) = S̄ ×_{G^ab} Z^{c/G}; K(G, c) = ker(U(G, c) → G), with [x] = (x̂, e_x). The group Ẑ^× acts on the set K(G, c) by α*(g, m) = (g^α W_α(m), m^α), with W_α(γ) = x̂_γ^{−α} (x_γ^α)^. The sets K(G,c)⟨−1⟩, Z^{c/G}_{≥M}⟨−1⟩ and 𝔖^{c,G} (Ẑ^×-orbits) are as in §12. Z^{c/G}_{≡q} is the set of m ∈ Z^{c/G} whose coordinates are constant on the q-th-power orbits of c/G. Z^{c/G}_{≡q,n,≥M} adds that every coordinate is ≥ M and the coordinates sum to n (p. 50).
items.note: PAPER-WOOD-19 proposes the Part II InductionRestrictionPartIIReducedSchur for exactly these (reduced Schur multiplier, reduced cover, universal marked extension, discrete power action).

items.name: Lemma 12.10: compatible Schur covers for H⋊Γ → Γ
items.statement: Let H be an admissible |Γ|′-Γ-group and G = H⋊Γ. There are Schur covering groups S → G and S_Γ → Γ with S → S_Γ over G → Γ, and ρ : H_2(G, Z) → H_2(Γ, Z) has kernel of order prime to |Γ|.
items.locator: Lemma 12.10 and its proof, p. 53 (arXiv v2)
items.note: Splits M = H_2(G) into its |H|- and |Γ|-primary parts; ker ρ is the |H|-primary part. H must be finite; the proof uses only (|H|, |Γ|) = 1, not admissibility.

items.name: Theorem 12.1 and Corollary 12.2: the lifting invariant of components
items.statement: For every algebraically closed k of characteristic prime to |G| and k-point s̄ of 𝓗ur^n_{G,c} there is a lifting invariant 𝔷_s̄ ∈ K(G, c)_{n,≥0}⟨−1⟩_k, compatible with specialization (across fields, via an isomorphism of Ẑ(1)'s; over a fixed k, the identity) and with Frobenius: 𝔷_{Frob(s̄)}(ζ) = q^{−1} * 𝔷_s̄(ζ). Hence points of one component share the lifting invariant, and geometric points of one component of 𝓗ur^n_{G,c} share its image in 𝔖^{c,G} (Corollary 12.2).
items.locator: Theorem 12.1, p. 48 (arXiv v2), and Corollary 12.2, p. 48
items.note: Wood, Res. Math. Sci. 8 (2021), Theorems 5.2, 2.5, 6.1 and §6.1. PAPER-WOOD-19 routes the analogous component invariant and its specialization compatibility to IG.5 (its items /80, /135).

items.name: Theorem 12.4 and Corollary 12.6: complex components as braid orbits, labelled by lifting invariants
items.statement: Over C, with standard generators γ_i of π_1(P^1 ∖ {P_i}, ∞), the fiber of 𝓗ur^n_{G,c} over P is {(g_1,…,g_n) ∈ c^n : g_1⋯g_n = 1, ⟨g_i⟩ = G}; there is ζ such that each point has lifting invariant ζ ↦ [g_1]⋯[g_n]; and π_1(Conf^n A^1(C)) = B_n acts by σ_i(g) = (…, g_i g_{i+1} g_i^{−1}, g_i, …), so components ↔ B_n-orbits (Theorem 12.4, via Fried–Völklein). Corollary 12.6: the lifting invariant bijects the components of Y_C, and of Y_{F̄_q}, having a given 𝔖-invariant in 𝔖^{c,G}_{n,≥M} with the lifting invariants over it.
items.locator: Theorem 12.4, p. 49 (arXiv v2), and Corollary 12.6, p. 50
items.note: The F̄_q half of Corollary 12.6 uses Wood 2021, Remark 5.4 (every lifting invariant occurs over F̄_q) and Lemma 10.3 with i = 2n. Theorem 12.4 rests on Fried–Völklein §1.4.

items.name: Theorem 12.5: stable braid orbits are classified by the lifting invariant
items.statement: (Wood, Res. Math. Sci. 8 (2021), Theorem 3.1.) For finite G and c as in Notation 10.1 there is M such that (g_1, …, g_n) ↦ [g_1]⋯[g_n] maps c^{n,G}_{1,≥M} (generating tuples with product 1 in which every class of c/G occurs at least M times) onto K(G, c)_{n,≥M} for every n ≥ M, with fibers exactly the B_n-orbits.
items.locator: Theorem 12.5, p. 49 (arXiv v2)
items.note: A purely group-theoretic statement; PAPER-WOOD-19 routes the same stable braid-orbit classification (its item /134) to IG.3.

items.name: Proposition 12.7 and Corollary 12.9: counting Frobenius-fixed components
items.statement: For q prime to |G| and n ≥ 1, b(G,c,q,n) = Σ_{m ∈ ker(Z^{c/G}_{≡q,n,≥0} → G^ab)} nr_{q−1}(W_{q^{−1}}(m)) (nr_k(a) the number of k-th roots of a), π_{G,c}(q,n) = b(G,c,q,n) + O_G(n^{d_{G,c}(q)−2}), and b = 0 ⇒ π_{G,c}(q,n) = 0 (Proposition 12.7). The text allows n = 0, where the formula fails (sourceIssues E25). The O_G constants are uniform in q and n. For each a ∈ (Z/|G|²)^× there are M_a, a non-empty set E_a of residues and r_{a,b} > 0 with π_{G,c}(q,n) = 0 if n mod M_a ∉ E_a and = r_{a,b} n^{d_{G,c}(q)−1} + O_G(n^{d_{G,c}(q)−2}) if n ≡ b ∈ E_a, for q ≡ a mod |G|² (Corollary 12.9).
items.locator: Proposition 12.7, p. 50 (arXiv v2), proof pp. 50–51, and Corollary 12.9, p. 52
items.note: π_{G,c}(q,n) is the number of Frobenius-fixed components of (𝓗ur^n_{G,c})_{F̄_q}, and d_{G,c}(q) the number of q-power orbits on the non-trivial classes in c. Z^{c/G}_{≡q,n,≥0} is defined in item 35. The component bound uses Ellenberg–Venkatesh 2005, Lemma 3.3. The proof writes d_G for d_{G,c} (E26).

items.name: Theorem 10.4: G-components versus Γ-components
items.statement: Let H be a finite admissible Γ-group, G = H⋊Γ and c the non-identity elements of G of the same order as their image in Γ (as in Lemma 10.2; E17). There is C_G > 0 and, for each a ∈ (Z/|G|²)^×, M_a and a non-empty set E_a of residues such that for all n and prime powers q ≡ a mod |G|² with gcd(q(q−1), |H|) = 1: π_{G,c}(q,n) = π_Γ(q,n) + O_G(n^{d_Γ(q)−2}); if n mod M_a ∉ E_a then π_{G,c}(q,n) = π_Γ(q,n) = 0; and if n mod M_a ∈ E_a and n is large, π_Γ(q,n) ≥ C_G n^{d_Γ(q)−1}. Here π_{G,c}(q,n) is the number of Frobenius-fixed components of (𝓗ur^n_{G,c})_{F̄_q}, d_{G,c}(q) is the number of q-th-power orbits on the non-trivial G-conjugacy classes in c, and π_Γ = π_{Γ,Γ∖1}, d_Γ = d_{Γ,Γ∖1}. The O_G constants are uniform in q and n.
items.locator: Theorem 10.4, pp. 39–40 (arXiv v2), proof on pp. 54–55 using Lemma 12.10 (p. 53)
items.note: b(G,c,q,n) = b(Γ, Γ∖1, q, n), from Lemma 12.10, G^ab ≅ Γ^ab (H admissible), the bijection c/G ↔ (Γ∖1)/Γ, and a kernel of order prime to q−1. The hypothesis gcd(q−1, |H|) = 1 is needed. For Γ = Z/2 and H = F_3² with inversion, H_2(G, c) = Z/3, and b(G,c,q,n) = 3·b(Γ,Γ∖1,q,n) when q ≡ 1 mod 3: generating 6-tuples of involutions with product 1 form 3 braid orbits. The proof writes S̄^i := H_2(G_i, Z)/Q_{c_i} for S^i/τ(Q_{c_i}) (E15) and π_G for π_{G,c} (E26).

items.name: Lemma 12.8: lattice points on a hyperplane in the positive orthant
items.statement: Let L = v + Λ ⊂ Z^d be a translate of a full lattice by an integer vector, and let a_1, …, a_d be positive integers. There are k ≥ 1, a residue s mod k and r > 0 such that L′(n) = L ∩ {Σ a_i x_i = n} is empty unless n ≡ s mod k, and then #(L′(n) ∩ {x_i ≥ 0}) = r n^{d−1} + O_{d,L,a}(n^{d−2}). The text allows non-negative a_i, not all 0; with some a_i = 0 the count is infinite (sourceIssues E8).
items.locator: Lemma 12.8, pp. 51–52 (arXiv v2)
items.note: An application of Davenport's principle (Lipschitz) after projecting away one coordinate. Explicitly k = gcd φ(Λ) with φ(x) = Σ a_i x_i, s = φ(v), and r = k/((d−1)! ∏ a_i [Z^d : Λ]); checked on two examples. Corollary 12.9 uses it with a_i the sizes of q-power orbits, which are ≥ 1.

items.name: Free profinite (pro-𝒞, pro-p) groups and pro-p presentations
items.statement: Free pro-|Γ|′ groups on finite sets and their pro-𝒞 completions. Minimal presentations of pro-p groups: a set generates the relation module R as a closed normal subgroup iff it generates R/R* (NSW Corollary 3.9.3). The generator and relation ranks d(G) = dim H¹(G, F_p) and r(G) = dim H²(G, F_p) are used through the p-covering group of §7.2.
items.note: The upstream ProfiniteProPGroups roadmap plans free pro-p and pro-𝒞 groups on finite sets for a structured class 𝒞 (Layer 4; the prime-to-|Γ| groups form such a class) and presentations with rank interpretations (Layer 5).

items.name: Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula and Deligne's weight bound
items.statement: For a scheme Z over F_q, #Z(F_q) = Σ_j (−1)^j Tr(Frob | H^j_{c,ét}(Z_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ)); for Z of dimension n the trace on H^{2n}_c is q^n times the number of Frobenius-fixed n-dimensional components; and every Frobenius eigenvalue on H^j_c has absolute value ≤ q^{j/2} (Deligne, Weil II, Théorème 1).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 1.4, p. 40
items.note: Following PAPER-WOOD-19: the trace formula for rational point counts is planned in SF.2 (integrating CohomologicalPointCounting), the top-degree trace on one component in EDC.2 (pairings), and Deligne's bound (H^i_c of weight ≤ i) in DWP.7.

items.name: Haar probability measure on compact groups; Carathéodory extension; Fatou and dominated convergence
items.statement: Haar probability measure on the compact group 𝓕_n (for random relations); Carathéodory extension of a countably additive premeasure from the algebra generated by basic opens; Fatou's lemma and dominated convergence; Tannery's theorem (limits of sums, Lemma 5.10); and the Portmanteau criterion (μ(U) ≤ liminf μ_n(U) for open U implies weak convergence, §5.3).
items.locator: Definition 3.15 and §5, pp. 17, 29–30
items.note: Mathlib (Measure/Haar/Basic.lean): haarMeasure K₀ normalized by haarMeasure_self. The probability Haar measure on the compact group is haarMeasure ⊤ (TopologicalSpace.PositiveCompacts.coe_top); Measure.haar has an arbitrary normalization. Also in Mathlib: MeasureTheory.AddContent.measure (OuterMeasure/OfAddContent.lean), the Carathéodory extension of a σ-subadditive content on a semiring; MeasureTheory.lintegral_liminf_le (Fatou); MeasureTheory.tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence; tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence (Analysis/Normed/Group/Tannery.lean); and MeasureTheory.tendsto_of_forall_isOpen_le_liminf (Measure/Portmanteau.lean).

routes.reason: IG.4 owns embedding problems with local constraints. PAPER-WOOD-19 routes the analogous facts there (its 'No everywhere-unramified split-infinity extension of the base', the global lifting-invariant input and marked extensions). The Galois-side inputs of LWZB belong there too: the Γ-action on Gal(K^#/K) (Definition 2.1), admissibility of unramified Galois groups (Proposition 2.2), and Property E for Gal(K^#/K) via the central embedding problem and a global character (Theorem 2.5, Lemmas 2.6–2.7).

IG.5 owns Hurwitz moduli, braid/Nielsen components and tame reduction. PAPER-WOOD-19 already routes the marked Hurwitz scheme, its rational points, lifting-invariant components, specialization and the Betti comparison there, and PAPER-ELLENBERG-VENKATESH-WESTERLAND-16 routes its Hurwitz-space inputs to IG.3 and IG.5. LWZB's Hurwitz schemes 𝓗ur^n_{G,c}, the analytic and topological comparisons, the point and component counts (Lemmas 10.2–10.3, 11.8, Theorems 12.1, 12.4, Proposition 12.7, Corollaries 12.2, 12.6, 12.9) and the G-versus-Γ comparison (Theorem 10.4) are instances.

IG.3 owns the braid action on generating tuples with product one. PAPER-WOOD-19 routes the stable braid-orbit classification by the lifting invariant (its item /134) there, and LWZB's Theorem 12.5 quotes the same theorem.

ST.5 owns function-field analogues, higher moments and the measures on the limiting space. PAPER-WOOD-19 and PAPER-ELLENBERG-VENKATESH-WESTERLAND-16 route their function-field moment theorems there. LWZB's Theorem 1.4 and Corollary 1.5, with the counting dictionary of Lemmas 9.1 and 9.3, are the same kind of statement.

RS-07 narrows ST.2 to arithmetic-family counts and names GN.4 as the supplier of generic lattice-point estimates and Davenport counting, and PAPER-BHARGAVA-SHANKAR-WANG-25 routes Davenport's lemma to GN.4. Lemma 12.8 (lattice points of a translated lattice on a hyperplane in the positive orthant) is a generic count of this kind.

routes.title: Induction, restriction, and Mackey theory for finite groups, Part II: reduced Schur covers and marked extensions
routes.brief: Coalesce with the candidate proposed by PAPER-WOOD-19 (same id and title), which already owns the reduced Schur multiplier H_2(G, c) = H_2(G, Z)/Q_c, the reduced Schur cover, the universal marked central extension U(G, c) = S̄ ×_{G^ab} Z^{c/G} with kernel K(G, c), and the discrete Ẑ^×-power action α*(g, m) = (g^α W_α(m), m^α). Add from Liu–Wood–Zureick-Brown (Invent. Math. 237 (2024), §12): the notation K(G, c)_{n,≥M}⟨−1⟩, Z^{c/G}_{≡q} and 𝔖^{c,G}, and Lemma 12.10. That lemma says: for H an admissible |Γ|′-Γ-group and G = H⋊Γ, there are Schur covers S → G and S_Γ → Γ compatible with G → Γ, and H_2(G, Z) → H_2(Γ, Z) has kernel of order prime to |Γ|. Also add the consequence that H_2(G, c) → H_2(Γ, Γ∖1) is surjective with kernel of |H|-primary order and compatible W_{q^{−1}} maps. Import ordinary Schur covers and factor sets from the upstream Layer 7; do not rebuild them.
routes.reason: WOOD-19's candidate is the single owner of reduced multipliers and marked central extensions; LWZB uses exactly these objects and one new compatibility lemma.

routes.title: Arithmetic statistics, counting fields and Selmer distributions, Part II: random Γ-groups and nonabelian Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet heuristics
routes.reason: ST.0–ST.5 plan families, measures, class-group moments and function-field analogues, but no theory of random profinite groups with Γ-action. The free admissible Γ-group, Property E, measures on profinite Γ-groups, Γ-chief factor pairs, no escape of mass and moment computations are new layers in the direction of arithmetic statistics. The upstream Profinite and pro-p groups roadmap supplies only free groups and presentations, not their random quotients or limiting measures.

Equivalently, λ(𝒞, H, G) = 0 for every G ∈ 𝒜_H on which Γ acts trivially. When the hypothesis fails, Prob((X_{u,n})^𝒞 ≅ H) = 0 for every n, and μ_u(U_{𝒞,H}) = μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) = 0. sourceIssues.reason: 𝒜_H contains Z/p with trivial H⋊Γ-action. §7.1 speaks of "G ∈ A_H with trivial H-action", and (4.13) needs it. For such G, |Y(G)| = 1, and every sub-H-extension D of an admissible E has Y(D) = Y(E), hence D = E. So Corollary 4.8 gives (h^m − 1)/(h − 1) = Σ_E 1/|Aut_{Γ,H}(E, π)| with m independent of n, i.e. h^m = 1 + λ by (4.10). Hence (4.17) fails whenever λ ≠ 0. The finite-n formula (4.13) is right: its k = 0 factor 1 − 1/|Y(G)|^{n+u} vanishes, so the probability is 0 for every n. It must be: by Proposition 3.13 every (X_{u,n})^𝒞 has Property E, and λ ≠ 0 for such a G exactly when H has a non-split central level-𝒞 Γ-extension by Z/p with trivial action. The limit formula instead contributes ∏_{i≥1}(1 − λh^{−i}), which is never 0. Example: Γ = Z/2, p = 3, 𝒞 the 3-Γ-groups of 3-class ≤ 2, H = F_3² with σ = −1.
